findings.text: This header publishes verifier data layouts and small inline utilities for log checks, subprogram lookup, call classification, per instruction flags, trampoline keys, stack slot math, spill and null tests, tristate constancy, backtrack masks and base type masking.
A compact index collection holds a signed entry count followed by a trailing flexible sequence of word sized slots used for successor sets, branch targets and similar lists.

Per instruction verifier scratch offers one active meaning chosen by opcode context: a register pointer classification for memory operations, a map pointer state, a preserved call operand, an arithmetic bound for pointer arithmetic, a map slot plus byte displacement pair, a type variable descriptor combining a register classification with either a type system handle plus identifier or a plain byte extent, and inline loop tracking state.

The same per instruction record carries a second selector for object creation size versus insertion displacement, a jump table reference for dynamic branches, a kernel pointer metadata reference, a constant key tracker for map lookups, a context field extent that may be empty, a pass marker recording last processing round, speculation guards for unsafe execution and unsafe results, zero extension hints for destination handling and arithmetic needs, plus markers for sleepable context, iterator stepping, per CPU allocation use, arithmetic state and fastcall spill pattern accounting.

Stable per instruction attributes include the original program position, individual bit markers for jump handling, pruning, forced checkpoints, callback use and direct or indirect targeting, a strongly connected component identifier with zero meaning singleton, liveness of registers on entry, and a precomputed constant register cache distinguishing scalar values, map references and subprogram references with a stored value per general register.
A single program may reference at most 64 [CITED] maps and 64 [CITED] type system objects.

The verifier log window tracks logical start and finish positions, a user space destination, a verbosity level, cumulative and maximum extents, and a kernel side temporary staging area sized by the temporary log constant.

Temporary log staging holds 1024 [CITED] bytes. Verbosity uses level one value 1 [CITED], level two value 2 [CITED], statistics value 4 [CITED] and fixed output value 8 [CITED]. The combined level groups the two level bits, the overall mask groups level plus statistics plus fixed, the kernel internal marker is the successor of the mask, minimum alignment is 8 [CITED] and preferred alignment is 40 [CITED].
User side log configuration supplies a user space buffer, its extent, a verbosity level, an offset where the true size is reported, and an opaque attribute reference.
A program may contain up to 256 [CITED] subprograms.

A subprogram argument descriptor pairs an argument classification with either a memory extent or a type identifier. Private stack handling is a three state knowledge value covering unknown, absent and adaptive modes.

Subprogram metadata records an optional name, entry position, line info index, postorder base, representative exit position, worst case stack use plus extra reservation, total and self instruction counts, fastcall spill base, boolean style properties for tail calls and reachability, throw possibility, absolute load use, callback roles including asynchronous and exception variants, argument caching, fastcall retention, packet data mutation and sleep possibility, a small argument count, private stack mode, per argument descriptors, and incoming plus outgoing stack argument tallies.
A call summary records parameter count with voidness and fastcall properties.

Liveness backtracking keeps a verifier reference, a frame index, and per frame masks for registers, stack slots and stack passed arguments. Identifier remapping uses a generator plus a bounded old to new table, while identifier sets store bounded identifier plus use count entries.

Strongly connected component tracking chains call sites leading into a component with the component identifier as terminator, links backedge records each holding a successor plus a full verifier snapshot, groups a call chain with an entry snapshot and a backedge list plus its length, and stores a visit count followed by a flexible visit sequence.
A descriptor array slot holds exactly one active view: a map reference, a type system reference, or an opaque scalar value.

The verifier context tracks current and previous instruction positions, the program under review, operation hooks, the owning module for attach type information, a work stack of states to explore with its depth, strict alignment and testing toggles, the active state, explored state buckets plus a reusable state pool, tables of referenced maps and type objects with their tallies, relocation maps for instruction arrays, an identifier generator, hidden subprogram and exception callback bookkeeping, and exploration plus safety toggles for arithmetic limits, pointer leaks, uninitialized stack use, privilege, speculation bypass, direct writes, exceptions and signature mode.

The same context stores per instruction auxiliary records with their length, previous line information, the log window, diagnostic storage, subprogram descriptors with extra slots for synthetic entries plus a leaf first ordering, scratch space reusable as either an identifier map or set, control flow work vectors for traversal order and postorder with stack and cursor positions, backtrack masks, current history linkage, per callsite argument snapshots, and pass plus subprogram tallies.

Remaining verifier context covers processed instruction and branch tallies with previous pass copies, worst stack depth, total time, per instruction state limits with total and peak allocation counts, longest liveness walk, pool sizes and backedge counts, dual shape descriptor array handling with resolved table plus count versus raw user reference, scratch tracking for registers and stack slots since last print, log cursor positions, scalar simulation buffers, branch simulation register copies, temporary text and argument name staging, instruction and epilogue staging, call chain scratch, liveness data, per component visit tables with component count, and successor plus dynamic branch scratch lists.

Descriptor array input appears in exactly one of two mutually exclusive shapes: a dense form where the caller supplies a count and every entry is resolved up front into an indexed table, or a sparse form with no table where entries are fetched from the raw caller reference and resolved on demand.

An untouched log window starts at zero. Once truncation begins the finish equals start plus cumulative length except during resets where the visible span may shrink below cumulative length, so visible content is finish minus start.

Constant register knowledge separates scalar constants fitting in a word, map references resolved through the used map table, and subprogram references resolved by subprogram number, with a stored word per register populated by a dedicated pre pass.

Small accessors report whether logging is active from presence plus level, compute incoming stack passed argument count from total versus register passed allowance, fetch per subprogram auxiliary and descriptor records, summarize calls by arity with void and fastcall traits, and distinguish helper, local pseudo and kernel function pseudo calls by opcode plus discriminator.

Per instruction markers set or query pruning, forced checkpoint, callback, jump point and jump target properties through the auxiliary table, while current context helpers select the active frame and its register file.

Trampoline keys pack an object identifier in the upper half with a type identifier below, using a distinguishing high bit when no target program is present, and unpacking recovers each half with masking. Stack slot derivation scales a negative byte offset by register width, and frame position resolves to the current index or the caller call site.

Spill tests recognize stack slots holding spilled registers and narrow to scalar spills, null tests detect scalar zero via tristate constancy, backtrack helpers set or query per frame register, slot and stack argument bits, and base type extraction masks away qualifier bits.

Hazards include speculative execution guards requiring barriers after unsafe results, optional allowances for pointer leaks and uninitialized stack reads or variable offset writes, speculation bypass toggles, and an internal bug path that warns once and appends to the verifier log.
Private stack knowledge starts unknown and settles to absent or adaptive as analysis learns whether an isolated stack region is required.

Component verification progresses from first entry through accumulating backedges to convergence per call chain, while log handling moves from untruncated through truncating to reset where visible span and cumulative length diverge.
The base type mask isolates the low portion of a type value as defined by the base type width.
